newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Week starts with bank FRCDs.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Week starts with bank FRCDs.

text.p: Asian debt markets started the week off quietly on Monday with news of a few bank floating rate certificate of deposit issues.
Bank of China announced that the FRCD for its Hong Kong branch has been 4.5 times oversubscribed.

"According to our preliminary counting, there are more than 60 financial institutions who have committed a total participation amount of over HK$9 billion, 4.5 times our issued amount," Bank of China said.
The five-year FRCD pays a margin of 35 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate and, with fees, an all-in return of 41.5 basis points to top-tier participants.
It was launched on September 16 with an initial amount of HK$2 billion.
Moody's Investors Service today assigned the issue a rating of Baa1, a rating that the Bank of China said it received with "regret."
"We are of the opinion that Moody's ratings are unfair and not objective," the bank said in a release.
Details were out on Asian Banking Corp's US$60 floating rate certificate of deposit issue, which launched late on Friday.

The certificates have a final maturity of five years but can be put or called after three. They pay a margin of 55 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate and, with fees, an all-in return of 70 basis points to the top tier.
Arrangers are KEB International, Bayerische Vereinsbank, Commercial Bank of Korea, Industrial Bank of Korea, LTCB Asia and WestLB Asia Pacific.

Indonesia's PT Bank Surya, acting through its Cayman Islands branch, has set a US$18.5 million FRCD. The deal has a maturity of 2.5 years and pays an all-in of 215 basis points to top tier participants.
NM Rothschild and Sons (Singapore) arranged the deal.

Bank Surya is an infrequent borrower. Its last FRCD was a two-year deal closed in November 1994. That transaction, launched through Rothschild and Indover Bank, paid an all-in return of 220 basis points.
Looking ahead this week, a couple of Philippines bank issues are on the outlook.
Arrangers Sakura Finance Asia and Citicorp International are expected to launch a US$100 million FRCD for Far East Bank and Trust.

The issue has a multi-tenor structure, with portions of the facility maturing in one, four and five years. Participants will be asked to participate on a more or less pro rata basis in the three maturities, bankers said.
Also expected this week is a three-year US$50 million FRCD for Rizal Banking Corp via LTCB Asia.
Japanese banks have been taking a closer look at Philippines' issues for a couple of reasons, bankers reported.
First, Japanese banks have been shying away from Korean and Thai bank paper, which had been the traditional beneficiaries of Japanese lending, in favor of higher-yielding credits.

Another key factor is the expectation that Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) will ease the 35 percent loan loss provision it imposes on Japanese banks lending to Philippines institutions when it reconsiders the issue early next year, bankers said.

"That such a heavy restriction will be taken away is good for Japanese banks lending to Philippines credits. In the point of view of bond underwriting it also is a positive factor," said a syndicate manager at a Japanese bank in Hong Kong.

Speculation that the major rating agencies will upgrade the Philippines also makes the country's credits attractive, he said. At present, the Philippines is rated Ba2 by Moody's Investors Service and BB by Standard and Poor's Corp.
"Another notch higher and the Philippines will be almost investment grade," the Japanese syndicated manager noted.
